name: Hits from the Sky: Comets, Asteroids and Craters
description: The belt of rocks between Mars and Jupiter, comets from the cold edge of the system, and the impacts that scarred planets and reshaped life.

checkpoints.name: Leftovers of creation
checkpoints.note: The asteroid belt, Ceres and the Kuiper Belt are leftovers of the solar system's formation. A planet-sized body, Theia, is thought to have hit the young Earth and made the Moon, and the Late Heavy Bombardment may have pelted both.

checkpoints.name: Scars on Earth
checkpoints.note: Vredefort and the Sudbury Basin are huge ancient impact structures. About 66 million years ago the Chicxulub impact led to the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction.

checkpoints.name: Watching comets
checkpoints.note: Meteor Crater in Arizona was formed about 50,000 years ago. Halley's Comet was recorded for centuries, and Edmond Halley showed that comets could return on a regular orbit.

checkpoints.name: Impacts seen
checkpoints.note: Biela's comet broke apart, the 1908 Tunguska event flattened Siberian forest, and in 1994 fragments of Shoemaker-Levy 9 struck Jupiter, watched by the Galileo spacecraft. Comet Hale-Bopp was a bright sight in 1997.

checkpoints.name: Landing on a comet
checkpoints.note: The Rosetta spacecraft reached Comet 67P in 2014 and put a lander on its surface, giving close views of how a comet is made and what it contains. Jupiter and the Moon, scarred by impacts, show how common such hits have been.
